title: Economy review of Experiment 8 replications
scope: Read-only primary-source research and local arithmetic. No GPU probe, model call, external rerun, or paid API call was made for this review. Reported external measurements were not independently benchmarked.

decision.active_run: Continue the already active frozen H100 worker with exact base-generation reuse, short scale-down and persistent compilation cache. Do not rerun completed calibrations.
decision.extra_gpu_probe: No extra paid GPU probe recommended for the remaining 12 passes at the review decision point and subsequent evaluation.
decision.reason: No reviewed source demonstrates lower all-in cost for a matched faithful run. A four-problem A100 probe cannot establish the cost of 128 simultaneous long generations; startup, steady-state throughput and memory-dependent batch capacity can differ.
decision.not_claimed: H100 is not proven cheapest. Continuing the active worker avoids a speculative migration whose savings remain unmeasured.
decision.future_candidate: A100-80GB is the least disruptive candidate for a future representative batch comparison because its memory capacity matches H100. Include startup, generation, idle scale-down and CPU/RAM in any comparison, and keep scientific scoring separate from hardware probes.
decision.protocol_constraints: Keep model revision, BF16, generation engine, thinking, sampling, full token/context limits and per-problem seeds fixed. Shorter caps, forced thinking closure, early loop aborts, quantization, changed subsets or editor hints are changed experiments.

rate_source.provenance: Function docstring records exact hourly rates obtained from Workspace.billing.rates() on 2026-11-03; displayed public per-second prices are rounded.

local_evidence.limitations: Summary cost_usd values are recorded estimates, not provider invoice measurements. Calibration seconds and external elapsed times do not establish identical startup or billing boundaries. These calibration generation seeds are seed 0; do not substitute their rows into live requests whose per-problem seeds differ.

cost_arithmetic.allocation: One GPU plus 4 physical CPU cores and 16 GiB RAM, Modal function rates, not sandbox rates.

formulas.break_even_duration_multiple: H100_hourly_total / candidate_hourly_total; candidate must finish strictly faster than this multiple to save money
formulas.all_in_cost: allocated_resource_hourly_total * billable_lifetime_seconds / 3600; add any other billed resources

cost_arithmetic.limitation: The equal-time amounts illustrate scale only. They are not measured or predicted A100 savings, and are not a task budget forecast. A100 slowdown reduces savings; lower-VRAM alternatives may require smaller batches.

external_sources.comparison: Closest reviewed throughput reference. Same think35 sampling and cap as local calibration; different samples, Transformers, GPU and potentially batch configuration. README example does not explicitly fix max_num_seqs; no evaluation script was found in its model repository.
external_sources.conclusion: The extrapolation is not a matched benchmark. Higher H200 hourly price and unknown billing boundaries prevent inferring a demonstrated all-in saving.

external_sources.comparison: Main comparisons use thinking off with an 8192-token cap or forced closure after 8192 thinking tokens followed by 4096 answer tokens. Full ordinary-thinking 32768-token MATH-500 figures are attributed to the original authors. The cap of the first-100 ordinary-thinking check is not established by that passage.
external_sources.conclusion: Establishes lower-memory GPU feasibility, not measured lower cost for the faithful protocol.

external_sources.comparison: Scripted mechanism replication with no frontier editor; different benchmark size, cap and engine. Free Kaggle quota is not evidence of lower billed Modal cost.
external_sources.conclusion: Not a replacement for the remaining faithful live-edit passes or full evaluation.

external_sources.comparison: Quantized engine, subset experiments, altered edits and different contexts/batches. GPU sampling is already used by current vLLM, so the published sampling gain is not an additional expected speedup here.
external_sources.conclusion: Useful implementation evidence, but no matched BF16/vLLM cloud-cost measurement.

external_sources.comparison: Different engine, subset, cap and termination policy. Evaluation seed shuffles problem selection; no generation seed appears in the request body. The quantized comparison changes observed accuracy.
external_sources.conclusion: No measured faithful cost advantage; early abort and quantization cannot be adopted as protocol-neutral savings.

verification.method: Inspected primary repository/card/article sources, resolved available immutable commits, read local calibration summaries and exact rate implementation, and recomputed arithmetic with Decimal. JSON structure, local hashes and arithmetic validated after writing.

h200_followup.scope: Read-only source comparison requested during the unchanged H100 run; no H200 probe, deployment, model call or billing mutation.

availability.limitation: A supported GPU type does not establish instantaneous account-specific capacity or queue time.

provider_rates.scope: Function resource rates, not sandbox rates. Exact provider hourly observation agrees with the rounded current public pricing page. Storage, network and other independently billed resources are outside this sum.

local_calibration.token_total_method: Sum token_count across every nonempty JSONL row; independently equal to n * mean_tokens in summary.json. Sample SHA256 matches the summary finished_metrics provenance.
local_calibration.duration_scope: Generator container accounting interval, including initialization accounted since worker entry; not pure decoding time or GPU utilization time.
local_calibration.cost_scope: List-price resource estimate including fixed margins, not provider invoice attribution.

external_comparison.timing_scope: Published elapsed-time scope does not establish matching initialization, queueing or billable-resource boundaries.

formulas.resource_hourly_total: GPU hourly + 4 * CPU core hourly + 16 * memory GiB hourly
formulas.h200_break_even_duration_multiple: H100 resource hourly total / H200 resource hourly total
formulas.h200_required_throughput_increase_fracti: H200 resource hourly total / H100 resource hourly total - 1
formulas.elapsed_window_cost: normalized or reported elapsed seconds * resource hourly total / 3600
formulas.illustrative_saving_fraction: 1 - H200 elapsed-window cost / H100 normalized elapsed-window cost

interpretation.assessment: H200 is a credible future candidate alongside A100-80GB. Its published throughput advantage exceeds its hourly premium in this unmatched comparison, suggesting an approximately 8.3 percent opportunity at equal generated-token volume. This is not demonstrated cost savings or a reason to change the active H100 run.
comparison_caveats: External token count is rounded; the two reported timing boundaries are not proven equivalent.
Both runs use BF16, vLLM 0.33, thinking enabled and the same think35 sampling and output cap; Transformers differs: local 5.17.0 versus external 5.20.2.
Local evaluation has one sample per problem and external evaluation four. Batch scheduling, max_num_seqs, checkpoint packaging and initialization can differ.
Equal-token normalization assumes throughput scales across workloads; different lengths, batch utilization and fixed overheads can invalidate that assumption.
The illustrative elapsed-window costs exclude added startup/scaledown margins. Do not compare the local margin-inclusive $1.251185 receipt directly with the external elapsed-only cost.

Current dispatch and rate code support H100 and A100-80GB. H200 adoption would require reviewed implementation support and representative validation; availability alone does not enable a configuration-only switch.
interpretation.active_run_decision: Keep the existing H100 worker unchanged.
interpretation.future_measurement: If later justified, compare representative work under unchanged model, sampling, seed and full-cap requirements, including initialization and scale-down in measured resource cost.
